core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Atopic Dermatitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Atopic Dermatitis: Thick emollient daily, topical Triamcinolone for flares, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: intensely itchy red dry patches in body folds

8-year-old boy presents with intensely itchy, dry, red, and scaly patches located in the creases of his elbows (antecubital fossa) and behind his knees (popliteal fossa). He frequently scratches them until they bleed.
reference_soap.objective: Excoriated, lichenified, erythematous plaques in the antecubital and popliteal fossae bilaterally. Skin is generally dry (xerosis). No signs of bacterial superinfection (no honey-crusting or purulence).
reference_soap.plan: Implement strict daily skin hydration with thick, fragrance-free ceramide emollients immediately after bathing. Prescribe a mid-potency topical corticosteroid (e.g., Triamcinolone 0.1% ointment) applied BID only to active flares for up to 2 weeks. Advise on avoiding triggers.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Atopic Dermatitis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Atopic Dermatitis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Thick emollient daily, topical Triamcinolone for flares

teaching.one_liner: A chronic itchy skin condition causing dry, red patches in the body's flexural folds.

must_ask.say: How long has this been going on?
